pr.title: Add explicit transaction handles and operation lifetime protection
pr.body:
Implements explicit synchronous transaction handles from litedb-org/LiteDB#3064 and #3067, including the native-admission stack from #132 (`49c327cf1`). This PR now targets **`dev` at `5dd942a73`**, already merged into the branch with the executable safety framework from litedb-org/LiteDB#3034/#3045.

## Safety / regression evidence

- **Contracts and risk:** High-risk ownership/concurrency change: `durable-ack`, `recovery-generation`, `reader-snapshot`, `historical-input`, `query-meaning`. Preserve native admission, storage formats, isolation and configured durability. New handle and disposal exception contracts are documented in the [migration guide](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/codex/transaction-handles/docs/transaction-handles.md).
- **Prior states and interactions:** Direct/Shared; legacy, ordinary and handle calls; live cursors and concurrent handles; pooled hosts; maintenance/close; encrypted and historical files; external writers; abandoned sessions; reused wrappers with fresh cores. Preserve inherited recovery, compatibility and fuzz coverage on the integrated stack.
- **Failure outcomes:** Acknowledged commits survive under the stated fault model; known rollbacks leak no writes; uncertain commits remain indeterminate. Cancel blocked admission before close drains actual work. Fence new operations for maintenance while admitting existing dependencies. Cleanup must not repeat a peer's fatal error or hide its own failure. External writes must be visible after reacquisition and cold reopen.
- **Evidence:** Eight real known-bad comparisons against `560529066` plus two inherited package proofs; permanent guards, registered fault hooks, explicit coverage dispositions and required platform evidence. [Audit and finite gate](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/codex/transaction-handles/docs/transaction-handles-safety-review.md). **Candidate `eb01f346e` is undergoing full CI against dev**: [CI/Safety evidence](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36698371646), [Regression proof](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36698371173), [Fuzz](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36698371190), [compatibility](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/actions/runs/36698371399). Earlier green results are not substituted for this candidate. The prior Windows x86/net8 opaque pin-test timeout is retained in the audit; its phase and product cause remain unknown. Policy checks pass against dev.
- **Coverage delta and residual concerns:** Three intentional test replacements and inherited CI/harness changes are accounted in the coverage ledger. No new quarantine or weakened assertions. The newly merged upstream close-checkpoint test now requires the exact surfaced IOException while retaining every WAL/recovery assertion; this intentional error-contract change is documented in the migration guide. Native-wait/pending-begin tests prove the admission path; Framework reuse, concurrent Direct handles and capability cases are added. Strongest counterexample: close/maintenance waiting on a continuation it prevents, including fatal shutdown and disposal races. Forced interleavings and independent review address it; tests cover exceptions/process death and inherited modeled persistence faults, not physical power removal. Existing quarantines and unrelated #3034 roadmap work remain explicit limits.

### Current implementation and review fixes

`BeginTransaction()` returns an independent handle whose collections, queries and readers stay bound across sequential thread handoff. Ordinary calls remain independent. Overlapping public use and callback reentry reject before execution; completed handles release their session/application graph.

Sequential Shared handles reuse the **holder worker and child SharedEngine wrapper**. **The storage core still closes/reopens, and native writer ownership is released between every transaction.** No coherent engine/page cache survives an external writer. Cleanup also releases idle data/log handles, coordination participation and the child's mode-admission lease. Changed password/serialized collation invalidates the wrapper. The worker pool retains at most two idle threads for one second.

The supplied review enumerated eight production findings (despite its nine-defect summary). All eight have fixes and permanent guards:

1. Shared close cancels blocked native admission before draining the legacy owner.
2. Pending maintenance blocks fresh readers while existing transaction/cursor dependencies finish.
3. Raw engine close wakes collection-lock waiters before draining; it preserves maintenance service generations.
4. Shared handle begin rejects caller-owned locking readers and pinned legacy ownership before scheduling.
5. Disposed reader/enumerator access validates again after admission but before abort handling, preserving prior writes even when disposal races the call. Real reader and disposal errors still fail the transaction.
6. Handle and child disposal coordinate with session close without masking an exception in a `using` block.
7. Cleanup distinguishes published fatal state from completed teardown and suppresses only the published peer error; its own I/O/invalid-data failures still propagate.
8. Writable ownership reclaims stale sort scratch without allowing read-only peers to delete active spills.

Fresh specialized review found the deferred-fatal variant of #7, a capture/disposal race in #5, and two evidence weaknesses; those were fixed and re-reviewed. The final child-admission review passed 36/36 cases on each net8/net10, adding eight forced plain/encrypted close-race cases. The new race guard fails on the actual previous head `3e88454e2`; twelve permanent variants distinguish rejected misuse from genuine failures. The final cleanup review passed 33 cases, including six independent variants. Its mutation control rejected broad error suppression. Earlier maintenance and Shared reviews also found no remaining in-scope defect. These are bounded reviews, not universal safety claims.

Final production source `3b60d5aea`: **220 handle/lifetime/abandonment/sort cases pass on each net8/net10**, with zero failures or skips. The independent child-admission review passed its 36-case selection on both runtimes. Counts overlap and are not summed. Relevant earlier integrated partitions passed 383 Shared and 200 native-admission cases per runtime. The maintenance/process-harness rerun passed 178 per runtime with one existing culture quarantine. Production Release builds pass all library targets. Hosted CLR4 and platform execution remains part of the current gate.

Checkpoint `2179ba651` passed all ten hosted regression proofs. Its platform runs exposed caller-owned test streams left open during cold reopen on macOS/Windows; fixed by closing the streams before verification. The earlier local process suite exposed obsolete reflection argument counts; fixed without removing process-death assertions. Failed attempts remain in the evidence archive. The superseded checkpoint CI was cancelled after the corrected candidate was pushed.

The full `1eaeaf092` suite additionally exposed the upstream close-checkpoint test's old expectation of a silently swallowed failure. `06c5b45ae` requires the exact original error and retains every recovery assertion; all eight checkpoint cases pass on net8/net10. No production change was needed. The superseded run and this semantic classification are retained.

The `06c5b45ae` Windows matrix caught a raw native-probe harness path containing a lexical `.` component, which is invalid after adding the Windows extended-path prefix. `52541f84d` probes the normalized filename, retaining both real alias-rejection checks and adding released-before/after controls. All 20 targeted cases pass on net8/net10; independent review found no weakened assertion. Candidate `3e88454e2` included this test-only correction. The later child-admission fix changes production code; its measurements were rerun on `3b60d5aea`. The superseded CI run was cancelled after the successor was pushed; its completed proof, fuzz and compatibility workflows passed.

The `3b60d5aea` native macOS Intel/net10 session exhausted its 300-second budget after 637 passing cases and one existing platform skip, with steady progress at the deadline; the same head completed all 642 cases on net8. Candidate `010821392` splits the exact original native selection into three checked, disjoint sessions, retaining the timeout and runtime/hook guards in each. Review also corrected case-sensitive discovery accounting to match VSTest’s case-insensitive selection: 21 lowercase-rebuild methods had executed but were absent from the old discovery record. These are CI/evidence defects, with the failed run retained. All 96 policy tests pass; no library code changes, dropped tests or unchanged rerun are involved. Both corrected macOS Intel jobs passed on this head. Its later Windows x86/net8 failure is separate: the legacy pin test gives child startup plus twenty independent commits one opaque 20-second wait. The log does not establish which phase stalled. Candidate `eb01f346e` separates child startup from actual write progress, preserves all twenty ordinary commits and keeps the pin owner alive. Only completed commits renew the 20-second progress deadline; a 60-second overall deadline remains. Plain/encrypted controls hold a real writer pin and require the probe to reject the blocked child. Exact cold records, payloads, indexed results and an unrelated sentinel are checked. All 15 focused cases pass on each net8/net10, and independent review found no remaining issue. The changed budget is explicitly recorded in the coverage ledger; no product-cause or green-CI claim is made.

### Final production measurements

Production Release/net10.0, `TestingEnabled=false`, measured source `3b60d5aea`, .NET 10.0.11, Ubuntu 24.04 x64/ext4, tiering disabled. Four alternating fresh-process rounds per case, five seconds warmup and five one-second measured windows. No local build/test/profile overlapped timing. Every result/index/sentinel and cold-reopen check passed; all windows retained. Rates are median process tx/s; ratios are medians of paired rates. Host load is uncontrolled. Changes after this measured source are limited to tests, CI/evidence recording and documentation; candidate `eb01f346e` has an identical `LiteDB/` tree.

| Reads/Shared handle | Pre-reuse head tx/s | Final tx/s | Paired gain | Head bytes/tx | Final bytes/tx |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 1,449 | 1,897 | 1.304× | 227,801 | 220,927 |
| 1 | 1,301 | 1,720 | 1.323× | 237,904 | 231,054 |
| 10 | 1,113 | 1,379 | 1.245× | 302,141 | 295,364 |

Baseline is pre-reuse PR head `c8c0cfab6`. **The historical 4.69× / 155 KB result was not reproduced.** Final one-read throughput improves 32.3% with 2.9% less managed allocation. This read-only transaction workload measures lifecycle cost, not durable-write throughput. Core/admission/coordination cleanup remains necessary.

Fresh comparison with upstream `dev` `5dd942a73` and stacked parent `49c327cf1`, same production setup and four alternating rounds per case (60 further processes):

| Workload | dev ops/s | Parent ops/s | Final ops/s | Paired vs dev | Paired vs parent |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Direct ordinary read | 93,691 | 88,180 | 82,509 | -11.8% | -6.9% |
| Direct legacy begin/read/commit | 93,973 | 85,814 | 72,641 | -23.8% | -15.1% |
| Direct attach/count/dispose | 7,133 | 16,632 | 10,999 | +53.7% | -33.5% |
| Shared ordinary read | 50,922 | 51,920 | 47,560 | -6.6% | -8.4% |
| Shared legacy begin/read/commit | 8,307 | 7,883 | 7,765 | -7.1% | -1.4% |

Read regressions remain explicit costs of the lifetime/ownership design. Ordinary Direct allocation is 10,112 / 10,264 / 10,248 bytes per operation (dev/parent/final), so allocation volume alone does not explain the cost. Attach benefits from #132’s pooled host against dev but still pays #133’s independent close machinery against its parent. Prior isolated guard/thread experiments and profiling are retained in the historical options report below; this PR adds no broader counter/guard/inline-close optimization. Performance acceptance is separate from the safety gate. All **84 comparison processes and 420 measured windows** are retained and verified; an immutable archive link follows after hosted validation completes.

### Public surface and compatibility


- Typed/BSON collections, queries, Include, vector queries, indexes and metadata are bound. Read-only Direct and Shared handles query and complete without granting writes.
- SQL, FileStorage and maintenance are not exposed on handles. Collection drop/rename and external/system query I/O reject before mutation; metadata `$cols`/`$indexes` is supported.
- Coordinated/custom/decorated engines inside `LiteDatabase`, Shared private memory/temp storage, and Shared caller data/log/temp streams reject handles. Direct caller streams remain supported. Ordinary/legacy provider support is unchanged.
- Existing `ILiteDatabase`/`ILiteEngine` implementers gain no required members. Concrete `BeginTransaction` plus optional provider/extension supplies the new capability.
- Legacy transaction signatures and valid synchronous behavior remain; CS0618 deprecates them with a warning. Warnings-as-errors projects can migrate with the documented targeted exception.
- Outcomes distinguish Committed, RolledBack, Failed and Indeterminate. Known committed outcomes survive cleanup failures; failed durable flushes never become a successful rollback. Original errors retain secondary cleanup diagnostics. Closed facade access rejects with `ObjectDisposedException`.
- Native admission, MMFs/sidecars, filesystem support, isolation, file formats and configured durability remain inherited from #132. Parameterless Shared begin keeps unbounded waiting; the new opt-in overload bounds both local/native writer waits and supports begin-only cancellation. Collection TIMEOUT remains separate.

[API, capability matrix, migration and close contract](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/codex/transaction-handles/docs/transaction-handles.md)


Only Shared holder/wrapper reuse is integrated as a performance option. Group commit, batching, IPC, native writer retention, storage-core caching, atomic SessionLifetime, single-bound-scope and inline-close experiments remain separate.

<details>
<summary>Historical options and proof branches (not current-candidate measurements)</summary>


### Historical independent performance options — separate proof branches

**Only the Shared holder + child-wrapper option is now integrated, with fresh measurements above. All other experiments remain separate and are not included. The numbers in this historical options section describe the original proof branches.** [Full report](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/blob/t3code/benchmark-group-commit-experiments/docs/transaction-performance-options.md), [controller source and replay instructions](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/t3code/benchmark-group-commit-experiments/tools/WriteControllerExperiments), and [raw results, traces, exact measured binaries and test evidence](https://github.com/litedb-org/LiteDB-Artifacts/tree/2d58276b767d82d01d894b3af6bceb5048f47bd1/pull-requests/JKamsker-LiteDB-133/2026-09-30-options). All comparisons use production Release/net10.0 with `TestingEnabled=false`, tiering disabled, the same Ubuntu/ext4 host, and alternating fresh-process order. Host load is uncontrolled; these are local descriptive results. No measured samples were discarded.

**Ownership experiments, each compared independently with the PR head:**

| Option | Measured effect | Assessment / proof branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reuse Shared holder threads | +25.5% one-read handle throughput; 1,302→1,634 tx/s | [Thread-only proof](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-shared-worker) |
| Reuse holder + child SharedEngine wrapper | **4.69× one-read throughput**, 1,302→6,064 tx/s; allocation 238→155 KB/tx. Zero reads 6.04×; ten reads 3.51× | [Original child proof; correctness fixes required](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-shared-child) |
| Atomic SessionLifetime admission | Direct ordinary +1.3%, Direct legacy +2.3%, Shared ordinary −1.4% | [Small/mixed result](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-session-refcount) |
| One bound context scope | Direct handles +1.7%, Shared handles +0.9% | [Small improvement](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-single-scope) |
| Inline idle close | Attach/count/dispose +41.3% | **[Rejected upper bound](https://github.com/JKamsker/LiteDB/tree/experiment/pr133-inline-close): fails the existing bounded-close regression.** Idle final release can still block. |

**The original child proof retained its Shared mode-admission lease and could retain mapped coordination participation. It also missed changed password/collation settings. The current integration fixes those differences; the final measurements above include those cleanup costs.**

The Shared proofs release native writer ownership between transactions. The child-wrapper cache is per originating session, and **the storage core still closes/reopens** so external writes are observed. Plain/encrypted interprocess tests verify writer progress, reuse, refreshed records and cold reopen. Retaining a coherent storage core across external writes remains a separate protocol change. Independent traces recorded 6,216 versus 9 thread-creation events for the head versus each reuse variant over about six seconds; these are event counts, not live threads or throughput. Most measured gain came from keeping the child wrapper beyond thread reuse alone.

Inspection also corrected the nested-guard hypothesis: Dispatch's `Session.Enter()` is an EngineContext thread-static scope, not another SessionLifetime monitor. The tested scope variant removes the redundant ordinary adapter only for internal TransactionEngine calls, preserving callback isolation and one-use dispatch authorization. Broad allocation pooling was not needed for the observed Shared allocation reduction.

**Durable-write baseline against dev:** one caller measured Direct 186.0→187.6 writes/s (+0.8% paired) and Shared 117.4→118.3 (+1.0%). Sixteen callers measured Direct −2.8% and Shared −1.1% paired. This small-insert workload does not show the large regression seen in reads. It differs from the older write table's updates to existing rows; compare within each matrix.

**Queued writes / separate-process IPC, PR-head library, sixteen callers:**

| Strategy | Writes/s | Median process p99 | Paired throughput vs Direct |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Direct ordinary | 164.0 | 394.3 ms | 1.00× |
| Shared ordinary | 113.9 | 168.0 ms | 0.69× |
| Existing CoordinatedEngine | 154.1 | 485.9 ms | 0.94× |
| Dedicated queue, one commit/request | 184.0 | 118.3 ms | 1.12× |
| Queue, batch cap 32, no linger | 2,008.1 | 40.5 ms | 12.22× |
| Queue, batch cap 32, 1ms linger | 2,152.9 | 39.4 ms | 13.16× |
| IPC queue, one commit/request | 182.7 | 120.7 ms | 1.11× |
| IPC queue, batch cap 32, 1ms linger | **2,078.4** | **37.2 ms** | **12.64×** |

Four fresh processes per strategy/caller count, three seconds warmup and five seconds measurement; every ID, payload, indexed result and unrelated sentinel is checked on two cold reopens. Single-caller Direct measured 187.0 writes/s; the zero-linger queue 186.7, the 1ms batching queue 154.6 and IPC batching 150.4. **Linger costs roughly 18–20% at low load.** Sampled peak WAL at sixteen callers is ~13.4 MiB Direct, ~13.1 MiB existing coordinator, ~8 MiB queued/IPC and <0.5 MiB Shared; checkpoint/close schedules and in-flight transactions differ. Full ranges, client/server CPU, allocation and drain measurements are in the report. IPC client allocation excludes the server.

**Semantics and limits:** this prototype coalesces immutable insert commands into **one atomic transaction per batch**, with one confirmed-WAL sync before acknowledgements. It does not group already-open independent transactions or separate WAL confirmations. One invalid duplicate rolls back its whole batch. Commit/I/O failure stops the writer; lost IPC replies remain indeterminate, with no automatic retry or durable inbox. Same-collection engine-level group commit requires a separate lock/publication/recovery design. The IPC proof owns exclusive Direct admission for its lifetime and only exposes writes; other processes cannot open ordinary Direct/Shared readers alongside it. A usable service needs a read/snapshot API or integration with the existing coordinator.

**Safety evidence:** 17 controller scenarios pass, including no early acknowledgement, exact commit-sync counting, batch rollback, queue saturation/drain, partial I/O and failed/post-sync errors, encrypted durable-image recovery, real process kills, truncated IPC frames and a durable write with a lost reply. The current library also passes 102 relevant storage/failure/process regressions. Viable library variants pass their relevant net8.0/net10.0 suites (116–149 tests per partition; child reuse also passes 82 Shared tests); all production library targets build. The naive inline-close failure is why that option is rejected. These are local Linux proofs, not Windows/macOS validation or hosted-CI claims for the alternative branches.

The archive retains all **240 measured processes**: 60 upstream comparisons, 84 ownership comparisons and 96 durable-write runs. These historical results motivated holder/wrapper reuse. The current implementation and fresh measurements are above; the other options remain separate.

</details>

baseCommit.message:
Make safety evidence and coverage accounting checkable in CI (#3034) (#3045)

Make the PR safety review and integrated regression audits of #3034 checkable:

- Safety section: every PR answers the five evidence prompts and names each
  contract its changed paths implicate (contracts.json, check_pr_section.py).
- Coverage accounting: removed tests, skips, weaker assertions, fixture, corpus,
  fuzz, fault-evidence and CI-config changes need a disposition added by the same
  change (coverage-ledger.json, check_coverage_regression.py).
- Fault-point registry: all 66 named hooks plus every DEBUG/TESTING delegate,
  with evidence that names its hook (fault-points.json, check_fault_points.py).
- Safety evidence job: required jobs, legs, revision, discovery completeness and
  never-executed tests are checked from the uploaded results.
- Regression proofs: a fix proves its repro against a real known-bad state
  (published package, dev commit or PR commit); known bad must fail and the PR
  head must pass. PRs labelled bug or bugfix-fix must add one. An informational
  Evidence check and advisory labels show tests added and proofs proven.
- Published-prerelease compatibility job, merge_group triggers, docs.
- Gaps closed: startup tail-trim and reclaim-lock hooks tested,
  SimulateDataWriteFail wired and tested, five never-run tests running again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
